## Overview

Two places in this repo render UI. The main surface is `packages/weft-devtools`, a private Chrome extension whose panel appears as a tab next to Elements and Console. The second is the default fallback of `AIErrorBoundary` in `packages/weft-react/src/AIErrorBoundary.tsx`, a light-themed alert box styled with inline literal values, shipped into other people's apps; it is a deliberate bypass surface with no tokens, and a consumer overrides it with the `fallback` prop. Every other package is a library with no UI. This document describes the panel, for developers debugging an agent run in a page they own. It is dense and quiet: small type, a narrow icon rail, a status strip, and colour reserved for state and the one accent.

The surface contract: the panel may not change the accent role or the meaning of success and error colours, and may not introduce a second palette. It may add tabs, and content components may choose their own layout inside the content area.

## Colors

The palette is a dark editor theme in one scope class, `.Weft-devtools-panel`: `bg` for the canvas, `bg-sidebar` and `bg-header` for the two chrome levels, `border` for every divider, `text` and `text-dim` for content and secondary content, and `accent` for the active tab, the status bar and focus. `success` and `error` carry state (connected, complete, failed) and are always paired with a label or icon, never used alone. Per-agent colours in the thinking view (`packages/weft-devtools/src/panel/components/ThinkingEntry.tsx`) and the graph edge and grid colours in `packages/weft-devtools/src/panel/components/ExecutionGraph.tsx` use literal values today and are not tokens; they are a known deviation (see Do's and Don'ts).

## Typography

The panel body uses the system UI sans stack at 12px. Data that is machine output (step data previews, timestamps, agent names in the thinking stream, step counters) uses `--font-mono`, a monospace stack. Sizes step 10, 11, 12 and 14px; section titles are 11px, uppercase, 600 weight, `text-dim`. Nothing in the panel is larger than 14px.

<!-- /GENERATED:typography -->

## Layout

The frame is a column: a 32px header, a main row, a 24px status bar. The main row is a 48px icon rail (36px square tab buttons) beside a scrolling content area with 16px padding. Spacing is built from 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16px; there is no spacing token yet. There are no breakpoints: the panel is a fixed-height DevTools pane (`100vh`, no page scroll), so content must scroll inside `content-area`. Icon-only tabs must keep an `aria-label`.

## Elevation & Depth

Depth is expressed by tonal steps (`bg`, `bg-sidebar`, `bg-header`) and 1px borders, never by shadow. A `--shadow-premium-1` token is declared but no CSS rule reads it. Five components carry a `shadow-premium-1` class name (`TimeTravelControls.tsx` among them) that no stylesheet defines, so it renders nothing; do not wire it up without recording why.

## Shapes

Controls and rail buttons use a 4px radius; status dots are circles (50%); the active-tab marker has a 2px trailing radius. The time-travel controls container is the one larger radius, at 8px.

## Components

There is no shared UI primitives directory and no variant files; components are plain React under `packages/weft-devtools/src/panel/components/`, styled by class names in `panel.css`. The tab rail is `TabNavigation`, the frame parts are `Header` and `StatusBar`, the run view is `ExecutionGraph` with `TimeTravelControls`, and `MetricsPanel`, `ExecutionHistory` and `WhatIfPanel` are the other tab bodies. Reuse these before adding a component that does the same job. Fifteen component files also use utility class names (`flex`, `text-zinc-500`, `bg-zinc-900`) that are not defined in `panel.css`, and the package declares no Tailwind dependency; treat that as an open styling defect, not a convention.

## Do's and Don'ts

**R1 DO take colours from the panel tokens.**
DON'T add literal hex or `rgba` values in components or CSS outside the token block.
Why: one palette keeps the panel consistent with the host DevTools theme.
Enforced-by: review. DEC: none.

**R2 DO pair a status colour with a label or icon.**
DON'T signal connection, success or failure by colour alone.
Why: colour-only state is unreadable for colour-blind users and in high-contrast modes.
Enforced-by: review. DEC: none.

**R3 DO use a monospace font for machine output.**
DON'T set trace data, ids or timestamps in the sans stack.
Why: alignment and scanability of run data.
Enforced-by: review. DEC: none.

**R4 DO give every icon-only control an accessible name.**
DON'T ship an icon button without `aria-label` or `title`.
Why: the rail is icon-only.
Enforced-by: review. DEC: none.

**R5 DO show real data or say the feature is not ready.**
DON'T display invented numbers as if they were measurements.
Why: `packages/weft-devtools/src/panel/DevToolsPanel.tsx` currently computes its metrics from fixed sample values, and the Thinking tab is a placeholder; a debugging tool that shows fabricated figures misleads.
Enforced-by: review. DEC: DEC-018.

## Drift Policy

A drift is a departure from an established pattern in this document. Every drift ends in exactly one of: conform (change the code to match) or record (append a DEC entry). Never silent. A design lint rule may be suppressed only with a DEC id in the suppression comment. Token values change through the CSS source, then regenerate; never edit a GENERATED block by hand.

Token source of truth: the custom properties in `packages/weft-devtools/src/panel/styles/panel.css`. Radius and spacing have no tokens, so their GENERATED blocks are empty; when tokens are added for them, regenerate and they fill in. Typography has one token, `--font-mono`, which the generator does not list, so its GENERATED block also reads empty.
